result.title: Creve Coeur Pension Fund Consulting RFP
result.summary: The City of Creve Coeur seeks an investment consultant to help its seven-member Employee Pension Board oversee the defined-benefit pension plan, which serves eligible full-time employees hired before June 1, 2006, including police employees. The fund has about $25 million in assets, allocated 70% to equities and 30% to fixed income; annual contributions are about $1.4 million and distributions $2 million. Commerce Trust manages, holds custody of, and pays fixed-income investments; Fiduciary Advisors consults on and manages equities. The plan has 146 members: 36 active, 81 retired, and 29 terminated vested. An actuarial report and investment policy are referenced. The City will review proposals and interview 3–5 firms; the RFP opens May 1, 2020, with proposals due May 21 at 2 p.m. Consultants should be independent, focused on consulting or investment management, knowledgeable across asset classes, supported by a team, able to process or coordinate pension payments, and experienced with governmental defined-benefit plans. Submit 10 hard copies and a digital version.

result.title: Core functions
result.summary:
Core functions
• Help us to develop and maintain our investment policy statement.
• Plan asset allocations annually and monitor regularly to keep us on track.• Recommend modification if there are significant changes in markets and bring to our attention any need or concern for changes.
• Provide research and recommendations for investments in each asset class.
• Follow recommended investments closely and meet with the Pension Board quarterly in person, monthly or as needed by phone.
• Provide monthly reporting of portfolio performance and statements.
• Work with our City staff to provide guidance in sourcing funds, opening new accounts, as well as tracking liquidity of investments for pension payments.
• Work with investment managers, funds and custodians to insure timely reporting of year-end financials as well as quarterly updates.

result.title: Profile of your Company
result.summary: A firm profile questionnaire requests information on the consultant’s mission, vision, values, organization, locations, staffing, consulting revenue, and clients’ municipal or pension plans and consulting-client counts. It asks whether the firm or affiliates are broker-dealers; where client assets are held and whether they are managed; key staff biographies, succession planning, service model, and relationship team; staff compensation and any investment-manager finder’s fees; conflict-of-interest and conduct policies; financial condition, ownership or restructuring changes, anticipated changes, and investment in the consulting division. It also asks about registered investment adviser status and Forms ADV I and II, fiduciary services, business litigation or other legal proceedings and their outcomes, negative press or social media issues, and levels of errors-and-omissions, fiduciary, and professional-liability insurance.

result.title: Scope of Consulting Services
result.summary: The RFP asks firms to describe their investment committee and members, investment philosophy, and approach to helping the Pension Board establish asset allocation, governance, investment policies and objectives, disciplined rebalancing, and tactical allocation changes. It requests capabilities in hedge funds, non-marketable alternatives, and private equity; views on index funds and ETFs versus active management; portfolio risk assessment; and tactical changes made in the past three years. It also asks about research and manager-search capabilities: research department structure, followed asset classes and recent additions or removals, asset-class performance, analyst staffing, manager evaluation methods and criteria, number of managers tracked, the fund’s manager-search process, and circumstances and reasons for manager terminations, including the number terminated in the past three years.

result.title: Monitoring and Measuring Performance
result.summary: The text requests information on performance monitoring and measurement, including use of model portfolios; client composite returns over one, three, and five years; comparisons with blended benchmarks and peer groups; access to peer data; GIPS compliance; and discretionary versus non-discretionary client proportions. It asks how performance is measured and audited, the firm’s benchmark philosophy and selection process, manager comparisons against benchmarks and peers, and whether blended benchmarks are recommended. For the Creve Coeur Pension, it requests recommended asset allocation and managers, their costs and absolute and risk-adjusted performance, and portfolio risk compared with the current portfolio. It also asks whether to revise the Investment Policy Statement, what performance software is used and whether it is proprietary or externally sourced and modifiable, when quarterly reports become available after quarter-end, and requests a comprehensive quarterly client report.

result.title: Miscellaneous
result.summary: The RFP asks firms to explain client transitions, including cost basis and performance data; disaster recovery and continuity plans; three competitive differentiators; a representative client list and five retirement-plan references (at least three government plans) with contacts and summaries; pension board education services; clients lost over the past three years and reasons; ESG initiatives or policies; and data-security safeguards. Proposals must provide detailed fees for all services, distinguishing fixed from asset-based charges and addressing investment-solution, management, trading, hidden, and other potential fees. Questions and proposals go to Lori Obermoeller, Director of Finance, City of Creve Coeur. Proposals must be submitted by email and hard copy, marked “RFP-Pension Fund Consulting Service,” to 300 N. New Ballas Road, Creve Coeur, MO 63141; 314-872-2519; lobermoeller@crevecoeurmo.gov.

result.title: Pension Consulting Proposal Requirements and Submission
result.summary: The proposal must include a representative client list and five retirement-plan references, at least three governmental, with contact details and plan summaries; describe services for educating Pension Board members; report clients lost in the past three years and why; and outline implemented or planned ESG policies and data-security measures. Provide a detailed fee schedule for all proposed services, including consulting, distinguishing fixed and asset-based fees and disclosing investment-solution, management, trading, hidden, and other potential fees. Direct questions and submit proposals by email and hard copy, marked “RFP-Pension Fund Consulting Service,” to Lori Obermoeller, Director of Finance, City of Creve Coeur, 300 N. New Ballas Road, Creve Coeur, MO 63141; 314-872-2519; lobermoeller@crevecoeurmo.gov.
